work_summary: Merged one more PR after the previous handoff: #312 (fix/live-chat-search-race, merged as 0c1919f) closed a race that #311 had introduced in the live-chat message search. #311 tagged each result set with the query that produced it so a stale set could not be DISPLAYED under a new term, but the older query's response still WROTE resultQuery when it arrived late, so the live term matched nothing and the panel stranded on 'No matching messages' until the field was edited. The guard needs a ref, not a state read: inside the effect closure searchQuery is the value from when the effect ran, so comparing searchQuery.trim() !== q compares q to itself and never fires. Also made searching derived (activeQuery !== resultQuery) instead of stored, because as state it could be cleared by a stale response and was false during the 300ms debounce so every new term flashed 'No matching messages', and added the catch the fetch never had. Verified by mounting the real component at the pre-fix commit (interrogator did this in a pinned worktree) and by frontend/.audit-probes/__tests__/search-race.test.tsx which asserts both directions. main is 0c1919f and green: CI, E2E, Encoding, CD all success, Deploy Frontend (Vercel) ran and Smoke Check Frontend passed. No open PRs, working tree clean.

THE RULE, PROBED, so nobody re-derives it: eslint-config-next 16.4.3 declares eslint-plugin-react-hooks ^7.1.0 where 16.1.1 declared ^7.0.0, so the bump forces plugin 7.1.1 which enables react-hooks/set-state-in-effect at the recommended preset. The rule rejects only a SYNCHRONOUS setState in an effect body. void (async () => { await load() })() passes with no cancellation flag at all. Calling a component-scoped useCallback that setStates from an effect body is rejected even when it awaits internally. Writing or reading ref.current during render is react-hooks/refs. A lazy useState initializer is fine.

LINT-CLEAN IS NOT A CORRECTNESS PROOF.
